chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Fadl al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud, from Sa'd, from Abu Umar al-Jallab, from al-Harith al-A'war, who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for Husayn, the one killed on the outskirts of Kufah. By Allah, it is as if I see the wild animals stretching their necks towards his grave, from various kinds of wild animals, weeping for him and mourning him by night until morning. When this happens, beware of neglecting (his grave).

key_terms.الْجَفَاء: Neglect / Hardness of heart / Lack of attention
key_terms.الْحُسَيْن: Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.), the grandson of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of wild animals weeping at the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic significance of Imam Husayn’s martyrdom, portraying wild animals as natural witnesses to his grief, which underscores the spiritual gravity of his sacrifice. The Prophet’s (or Imam Ali’s) warning against 'jafa' (spiritual hardness or insensitivity) links this physical phenomenon to the believers' internal state, urging them to maintain emotional and spiritual connection through regular ziyarah to prevent their hearts from becoming calloused.
